This relationship is supported by the shared indication of Mogamulizumab with the target condition, suggesting a potential mechanism of action that may be common across different subtypes of T-cell lymphoma. The evidence from the three paths indicates that Forodesine, through its indication on various T-cell lymphoma subtypes, leads to Mogamulizumab, which in turn is linked to the target condition. The overlapping indications and the presence of Mogamulizumab as a common mediator suggest that Forodesine may exert a therapeutic effect on T-cell lymphomas, possibly through a mechanism that involves the modulation of immune responses or other cellular pathways. The integration of these pathways highlights the potential for Forodesine to be a candidate for repurposing in the treatment of peripheral T-cell lymphoma, based on its association with a broad range of T-cell lymphoma subtypes.
